Unit 15 – Grammar

The passive · the causative · direct and indirect objects · 10 exercises

Exercise A – Choose the correct word or phrase
Choose the correct word in bold: was or has (passive forms).
  • 1. The prime minister criticised for his recent actions.
    ✓ was (past simple passive – specific past event)
  • 2. When I walked past the Wilsons' house, their new sofa being delivered.
    ✓ was (past continuous passive – happening at that time)
  • 3. Our teacher told us to take our favourite book to school tomorrow.
    ✓ has (present perfect passive – relevance to present/future)
  • 4. I think my mobile been stolen!
    ✓ has (present perfect passive – recent event with present relevance)
  • 5. Jonathan chosen to play the lead role in the school play.
    ✓ has (present perfect passive – result affecting now)
  • 6. I'm sleeping downstairs because my bedroom .
    ✓ is being painted (present continuous passive – happening now)
  • 7. This picture probably taken during the war.
    ✓ was (past simple passive – past time)
  • 8. Your essays must handed in on Friday morning.
    ✓ be (modal passive: must be handed in)
  • 9. Someone left their wallet on the floor.
    ✓ has (present perfect – unspecified past with present result)
  • 10. Did you hear about the bank robbed?
    ✓ being (passive gerund after about)
  • 11. Treasure Island written by Robert Louis Stevenson.
    ✓ was (historical past fact)
  • 12. It was a real shock when my dad fired from his job.
    ✓ was (past simple passive in when-clause)
  • 13. The Vikings had visited America before it discovered by Columbus.
    ✓ was (past simple passive in before-clause)
  • 14. When we got to the airport, we learned that our flight been delayed.
    ✓ had (past perfect passive – before arrival)
  • 15. your ticket for the concert tomorrow paid for by you or your parents?
    ✓ Was (past simple passive question)
Exercise B – Complete using the correct passive form of the verb in brackets
Write the correct passive form of the verb in brackets.
  • 1. The Earth (hold) by the gravity of the Sun and orbits around it.
    ✓ is held
  • 2. The first feature-length comedy film (create) by Charlie Chaplin.
    ✓ was created
  • 3. The award for best video (present) later this evening.
    ✓ will be presented
  • 4. By the time you read this, I (arrest) for murder.
    ✓ will have been arrested
  • 5. I don't know whether our tests (mark) yet or not.
    ✓ have been marked
  • 6. Radio waves (discover) by Marconi.
    ✓ was discovered
  • 7. You wouldn't think it to look at him now, but Jack (bully) when he was at school.
    ✓ was bullied
  • 8. Your application (consider) and we will let you know as soon as we've made a decision.
    ✓ is being considered
  • 9. The roof of the car (lower) by pressing this button here.
    ✓ can be lowered
  • 10. Our tent (blow) over in the night by the wind.
    ✓ was blown
  • 11. Chess (play) for around two thousand years now.
    ✓ has been played
  • 12. Two men (question) at this moment by police in connection with the burglary.
    ✓ are being questioned
Exercise C – Write sentences in the passive
Rewrite each set of prompts as a passive sentence. Write your answer in the box.
  • 1. Our car / service / a mechanic / at the moment.
    ✓ Our car is being serviced by a mechanic at the moment.
  • 2. A man / shoot / an air gun / outside the petrol station last night.
    ✓ A man was shot by an air gun outside the petrol station last night.
  • 3. Gunpowder / invent / the Chinese.
    ✓ Gunpowder was invented by the Chinese.
  • 4. At the surgery yesterday, I / examine / Dr Peterson / and I / give / a prescription.
    ✓ At the surgery yesterday, I was examined by Dr Peterson and given a prescription.
  • 5. I went to see it because I / tell / it was a good film / all my friends.
    ✓ I went to see it because I was told it was a good film by all my friends.
  • 6. This photograph / take / my grandfather.
    ✓ This photograph was taken by my grandfather.
  • 7. It looked like the window / break / a hammer / some time before.
    ✓ It looked like the window had been broken by a hammer some time before.
  • 8. Our dog / give / an injection / a special syringe / the vet.
    ✓ Our dog was given an injection with a special syringe by the vet.
  • 9. The winning goal in last night's match / score / Donatello / a brilliant free kick.
    ✓ The winning goal in last night's match was scored by Donatello with a brilliant free kick.
  • 10. Your cheque / send / last Friday and / should / deliver / to you tomorrow.
    ✓ Your cheque was sent last Friday and should be delivered to you tomorrow.
Exercise D – Rewrite using the phrase given
Rewrite each sentence using the phrase given in brackets.
  • 1. They have been building the new road for a long time now. (under construction)
    ✓ The new road has been under construction for a long time now.
  • 2. They had been training the horse for the race for over a year. (in training)
    ✓ The horse had been in training for the race for over a year.
  • 3. They have been discussing the issue in Parliament. (under discussion)
    ✓ The issue has been under discussion in Parliament.
  • 4. They had been observing the criminal for the past two weeks. (under observation)
    ✓ The criminal had been under observation for the past two weeks.
  • 5. They have been using this plane for over 25 years now. (in use)
    ✓ This plane has been in use for over 25 years now.
  • 6. They have been developing the Cyborg D423 robot for over ten years. (in development)
    ✓ The Cyborg D423 robot has been in development for over ten years.
Exercise E – Rewrite in the passive starting with the words given
Rewrite each sentence in the passive, starting with the words provided.
  • 1. People say that Bali is a beautiful island. → It …
    ✓ It is said that Bali is a beautiful island.
  • 2. People generally think that life won't be found on Mars. → It …
    ✓ It is generally thought that life won't be found on Mars.
  • 3. It is generally said that Christmas is too commercialised. → Christmas …
    ✓ Christmas is generally said to be too commercialised.
  • 4. People often argue that prison doesn't work. → It …
    ✓ It is often argued that prison doesn't work.
  • 5. People have suggested that the school should start to produce a magazine. → It …
    ✓ It has been suggested that the school should start to produce a magazine.
  • 6. People say that crocodile tastes like squid. → Crocodile …
    ✓ Crocodile is said to taste like squid.
  • 7. It is said that the Vikings discovered America before Columbus. → The Vikings …
    ✓ The Vikings are said to have discovered America before Columbus.
  • 8. People think that heart disease is caused by eating the wrong things. → Heart disease …
    ✓ Heart disease is thought to be caused by eating the wrong things.
Exercise F – Choose the correct answer
Choose the best option A, B, C or D for the causative (have/get something done).
  • 1. We ………… a swimming pool put in this week.
    ✓ B are having (causative: are having [something] put in)
  • 2. Why don't you get a doctor ………… at your arm?
    ✓ A to look (get + person + to-infinitive)
  • 3. My teeth were a little yellow so I ………… by the dentist.
    ✓ D had them cleaned (causative past: had + object + past participle)
  • 4. Stuart's thinking of having ………… !
    ✓ C his head shaved (have + object + past participle)
  • 5. My sister ………… her ear pierced last weekend.
    ✓ B got (got her ear pierced – causative with get)
  • 6. Mum and Dad didn't fancy cooking, so we got a pizza ………… .
    ✓ C delivered (get + object + past participle – causative)
  • 7. You should ………… a professional to check your house for earthquake damage.
    ✓ A have (have + person + infinitive without to)
  • 8. Kelly wanted to have a live band ………… at her wedding.
    ✓ C played (have + object + past participle)
  • 9. Can we ………… this summer?
    ✓ D have air-conditioning installed (have + object + past participle)
  • 10. We ………… while we were on holiday.
    ✓ B had our house burgled (causative of misfortune: had + object + past participle)

Complete each second sentence using the word given so that it has a similar meaning. Write between two and five words.
  • 1.
    Someone has scratched my car on the door! been
    My car on the door!
    ✓ has been scratched
  • 2.
    Tommy is having an operation right now. being
    Tommy right now.
    ✓ is being operated on

    Has Fiona invited you to her party? been
    Have party?
    ✓ you been invited to Fiona's

    Shakespeare probably wrote this play in 1587. written
    This play Shakespeare in 1587.
    ✓ was probably written by

    The government is considering a new law to ban smoking following new research. considered
    A new law to ban smoking new research.
    ✓ is being considered following

    My mum told me to go to Megagrocers. sent
    I my mum.
    ✓ was sent to Megagrocers by
  • 7.
    I didn't understand a word so I asked my teacher and she explained it to me. got
    I didn't understand a word so I it to me.
    ✓ got my teacher to explain

Exercise I – Rewrite with the indirect object at the end
Rewrite each sentence so that the indirect object comes at the end.
  • 1. My dad got me a great computer game!
    ✓ My dad got a great computer game for me.
  • 2. Dave sent Jill a really nice letter.
    ✓ Dave sent a really nice letter to Jill.
  • 3. I threw Colin the ball.
    ✓ I threw the ball to Colin.
  • 4. The waiter offered us a menu.
    ✓ The waiter offered a menu to us.
  • 5. The hotel provides its guests with satellite television.
    ✓ The hotel provides satellite television for its guests.
  • 6. My grandma taught me this song.
    ✓ My grandma taught this song to me.

Write exactly one word in each numbered gap.

The poor peasants were curious about the new plants and many of them (13) stolen to be planted in their own gardens. It was the start of French fries!
